-- | A strict linked list with stack-safe operations and reversed-order
--   helpers.
@package strict-list
@version 1.0.0.1


-- | Definitions of strict linked list.
--   
--   Most basic operations like <a>fmap</a>, <a>filter</a>,
--   <a>&lt;*&gt;</a> are implemented efficiently by producing an
--   intermediate list in reversed order and then reversing it to the
--   original order to avoid stack recursion. These intermediate reversed
--   functions are exposed by the API, because they very well may be useful
--   for efficient implementations of data-structures built on top of list.
--   E.g., the <a>"deque"</a> package exploits them heavily.
--   
--   One useful rule of thumb would be that whenever you see that a
--   function has a reversed counterpart, that counterpart is faster and
--   hence if you don't care about the order or intend to reverse the list
--   further down the line, you should give preference to that counterpart.
module StrictList

-- | Strict linked list.
data StrictList a
Cons :: !a -> !StrictList a -> StrictList a
Nil :: StrictList a

-- | Convert to lazy list.
toList :: StrictList a -> [a]

-- | Convert to lazy list in normal form (with all elements and spine
--   evaluated).
toListReversed :: StrictList a -> [a]

-- | Construct from a lazy list.
fromList :: [a] -> StrictList a

-- | Construct from a lazy list in reversed order.
fromListReversed :: [a] -> StrictList a

-- | Reverse the list.
reverse :: StrictList a -> StrictList a

-- | Leave only the specified amount of elements.
take :: Int -> StrictList a -> StrictList a

-- | Leave only the specified amount of elements, in reverse order.
takeReversed :: Int -> StrictList a -> StrictList a

-- | Leave only the elements after the specified amount of first elements.
drop :: Int -> StrictList a -> StrictList a

-- | Leave only the elements satisfying the predicate.
filter :: (a -> Bool) -> StrictList a -> StrictList a

-- | Leave only the elements satisfying the predicate, producing a list in
--   reversed order.
filterReversed :: (a -> Bool) -> StrictList a -> StrictList a

-- | Leave only the first elements satisfying the predicate.
takeWhile :: (a -> Bool) -> StrictList a -> StrictList a

-- | Leave only the first elements satisfying the predicate, producing a
--   list in reversed order.
takeWhileReversed :: (a -> Bool) -> StrictList a -> StrictList a

-- | Drop the first elements satisfying the predicate.
dropWhile :: (a -> Bool) -> StrictList a -> StrictList a

-- | Same as <tt>(<a>takeWhile</a> predicate . <a>reverse</a>)</tt>. E.g.,
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; takeWhileFromEnding (&gt; 2) (fromList [1,4,2,3,4,5])
--   fromList [5,4,3]
--   </pre>
takeWhileFromEnding :: (a -> Bool) -> StrictList a -> StrictList a

-- | Same as <tt>(<a>dropWhile</a> predicate . <a>reverse</a>)</tt>. E.g.,
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; dropWhileFromEnding (&gt; 2) (fromList [1,4,2,3,4,5])
--   fromList [2,4,1]
--   </pre>
dropWhileFromEnding :: (a -> Bool) -> StrictList a -> StrictList a

-- | An optimized version of the same predicate applied to <a>takeWhile</a>
--   and <a>dropWhile</a>. IOW,
--   
--   <pre>
--   span predicate list = (takeWhile predicate list, dropWhile predicate list)
--   </pre>
span :: (a -> Bool) -> StrictList a -> (StrictList a, StrictList a)

-- | Same as <a>span</a>, only with the first list in reverse order.
spanReversed :: (a -> Bool) -> StrictList a -> (StrictList a, StrictList a)

-- | Same as <tt>(<a>span</a> predicate . <a>reverse</a>)</tt>.
spanFromEnding :: (a -> Bool) -> StrictList a -> (StrictList a, StrictList a)

-- | An opposite version of <a>span</a>. I.e.,
--   
--   <pre>
--   break predicate = span (not . predicate)
--   </pre>
break :: (a -> Bool) -> StrictList a -> (StrictList a, StrictList a)

-- | Same as <a>break</a>, only with the first list in reverse order.
breakReversed :: (a -> Bool) -> StrictList a -> (StrictList a, StrictList a)

-- | Pattern match on list using functions.
--   
--   Allows to achieve all the same as <a>uncons</a> only without
--   intermediate <a>Maybe</a>.
--   
--   Essentially provides the same functionality as <tt>either</tt> for
--   <tt>Either</tt> and <tt>maybe</tt> for <a>Maybe</a>.
match :: result -> (element -> StrictList element -> result) -> StrictList element -> result

-- | Get the first element and the remainder of the list if it's not empty.
uncons :: StrictList a -> Maybe (a, StrictList a)

-- | Get the first element, if list is not empty.
head :: StrictList a -> Maybe a

-- | Get the last element, if list is not empty.
last :: StrictList a -> Maybe a

-- | Get all elements of the list but the first one.
tail :: StrictList a -> StrictList a

-- | Get all elements but the last one.
init :: StrictList a -> StrictList a

-- | Get all elements but the last one, producing the results in reverse
--   order.
initReversed :: StrictList a -> StrictList a

-- | Apply the functions in the left list to elements in the right one.
apZipping :: StrictList (a -> b) -> StrictList a -> StrictList b

-- | Apply the functions in the left list to elements in the right one,
--   producing a list of results in reversed order.
apZippingReversed :: StrictList (a -> b) -> StrictList a -> StrictList b

-- | Add elements of the left list in reverse order in the beginning of the
--   right list.
prependReversed :: StrictList a -> StrictList a -> StrictList a

-- | Map producing a list in reversed order.
mapReversed :: (a -> b) -> StrictList a -> StrictList b

-- | Apply the functions in the left list to every element in the right
--   one, producing a list of results in reversed order.
apReversed :: StrictList (a -> b) -> StrictList a -> StrictList b

-- | Use a function to produce a list of lists and then concat them
--   sequentially, producing the results in reversed order.
explodeReversed :: (a -> StrictList b) -> StrictList a -> StrictList b

-- | Join (concat) producing results in reversed order.
joinReversed :: StrictList (StrictList a) -> StrictList a

-- | Map and filter elements producing results in reversed order.
mapMaybeReversed :: (a -> Maybe b) -> StrictList a -> StrictList b

-- | Keep only the present values, reversing the order.
catMaybesReversed :: StrictList (Maybe a) -> StrictList a
instance Data.Functor.Alt.Alt StrictList.StrictList
instance GHC.Internal.Base.Alternative StrictList.StrictList
instance GHC.Internal.Base.Applicative StrictList.StrictList
instance Data.Functor.Bind.Class.Apply StrictList.StrictList
instance Test.QuickCheck.Arbitrary.Arbitrary1 StrictList.StrictList
instance Test.QuickCheck.Arbitrary.Arbitrary a => Test.QuickCheck.Arbitrary.Arbitrary (StrictList.StrictList a)
instance Data.Functor.Bind.Class.Bind StrictList.StrictList
instance GHC.Internal.Data.Data.Data a => GHC.Internal.Data.Data.Data (StrictList.StrictList a)
instance GHC.Classes.Eq a => GHC.Classes.Eq (StrictList.StrictList a)
instance GHC.Internal.Data.Foldable.Foldable StrictList.StrictList
instance GHC.Internal.Base.Functor StrictList.StrictList
instance GHC.Internal.Generics.Generic1 StrictList.StrictList
instance GHC.Internal.Generics.Generic (StrictList.StrictList a)
instance Data.Hashable.Class.Hashable a => Data.Hashable.Class.Hashable (StrictList.StrictList a)
instance GHC.Internal.IsList.IsList (StrictList.StrictList a)
instance GHC.Internal.Base.MonadPlus StrictList.StrictList
instance GHC.Internal.Base.Monad StrictList.StrictList
instance GHC.Internal.Base.Monoid (StrictList.StrictList a)
instance Control.DeepSeq.NFData1 StrictList.StrictList
instance Control.DeepSeq.NFData a => Control.DeepSeq.NFData (StrictList.StrictList a)
instance GHC.Classes.Ord a => GHC.Classes.Ord (StrictList.StrictList a)
instance Data.Functor.Plus.Plus StrictList.StrictList

instance GHC.Internal.Base.Semigroup (StrictList.StrictList a)

instance GHC.Internal.Data.Traversable.Traversable StrictList.StrictList
